name: ice-giant haze, with the geometric mean of the absorption retrieved from Uranus's and Neptune's spectra
paper: P. G. J. Irwin, N. A. Teanby, L. N. Fletcher, D. Toledo, G. S. Orton, M. H. Wong, M. T. Roman, S. Pérez-Hoyos, A. James and J. Dobinson, "Hazy blue worlds: A holistic aerosol model for Uranus and Neptune, including dark spots", J. Geophys. Res. Planets 127 (2022) e2022JE007189, DOI 10.1029/2022JE007189, its values read from the preprint, arXiv:2201.04516v2
source: the preprint's source, https://arxiv.org/e-print/2201.04516v2, SHA-256 9aac82980dd91c5dacc34d5552629e113cdb8e3fb7c6d39c3dd8f324fa045259, fetched 2026-10-14, its file Neptune_Uranus_Haze.tex, SHA-256 7061326a906a8d284d40bd0d2bf0b0991e7f4a1e398de9adf6d4bd3947b8aad9, the tables "Estimated n_imag spectra for Uranus aerosols" and "… for Neptune aerosols", the Aerosol-3 (extended haze) "Mean 1" columns; read as data
licence: Adapted from CC BY 4.0 material (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/): P. G. J. Irwin et al., J. Geophys. Res. Planets 127 (2022) e2022JE007189 (arXiv:2201.04516v2). Changed: the geometric mean of the two planets' Aerosol-3 k, reduced onto this grid, with n held at the paper's 1.4; this file is offered under CC BY 4.0
reduction: at each of the tables' wavelengths, every 100 nm over 300–1,900 nm, k is the geometric mean of Uranus's and Neptune's Aerosol-3 "Mean 1", since one key serves every ice giant; then n linear and k linear in log k in wavelength between the source's rows, onto 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures. The two planets differ by up to a factor of 29 over 300–800 nm (Uranus 1.50 × 10⁻³ and Neptune 1.01 × 10⁻² at 400 nm, 1.91 × 10⁻⁴ and 5.47 × 10⁻³ at 500 nm). n is the paper's 1.4, which its retrieval fixes at 800 nm and carries elsewhere by Kramers–Kronig (its §3.4 and §3.6); that shape is not reproduced, and n is 1.4 throughout
standIn: an effective index retrieved from the spectra of Uranus and Neptune for their unidentified photochemical haze, its k the geometric mean of the two planets' values, which differ by up to a factor of 29, and not a laboratory measurement
